title: Forward-only HTTP streams need retained delimiter lookahead
applies_when: A file-like HTTP wrapper inherits a delimiter reader that reads chunks and seeks backward after finding a newline, although the underlying response is forward-only.
lesson: Trace both how the delimiter is found and where over-read bytes go. A successful HTTP transfer and passing readlines() do not establish that readline() or iteration works: fsspec's bulk method reads to EOF, but its inherited per-line path seeks backward and fails on streaming responses. Compare the real transport with a BytesIO oracle, with forced streaming, unknown-size responses and seekable controls. Retain the unread suffix in the stream's read path and adjust the caller-visible position; later read/readinto/line calls must consume that suffix in order. Keep ordinary seekable behavior unchanged and continue rejecting user seeks on a forward-only response. Test delimiters spanning chunks, empty input, EOF, mixed reads, close and buffered controls before calling the change ready.
avoid_when: First establish that the wrapper promises the affected file-like operation; not every raw stream supports every IOBase method. Do not treat a separate read(None) normalization or optional readline(size) change as proof of this route. Do not replace real I/O with a seek-capable memory fake, enable arbitrary seeking or discard lookahead. Evaluate the overhead of a byte-by-byte fallback instead of assuming it is free, and do not assume extra buffering is fast without measurement. The evidence below is scoped native correctness and a submitted PR, not maintainer acceptance, full downstream/browser/CI coverage, performance or measured Scout yield/cost improvement.

evidence.note: readuntil rewinds an over-read chunk with seek; readline and iteration use that path, while readlines uses a whole-file read. A passing bulk-read control cannot establish per-line behavior.

Independent complete-source Windows3.14/Linux3.12 loopback checks each reproduce 12 streaming line/iteration failures and retain 12 bulk/seekable controls. This is not a failure introduced by the separate read(None) PR.

Exact 58-case native witness covers both HTTP backends, delimiter boundaries, mixed reads, position, EOF and close. On Linux the same cases change from 37 failed/21 passed on unchanged master to 58 passed, with no skips; all original passing controls remain passing.

Submitted Ready at bddbbf6; selected native suites report Linux747pass/22skip/1existing-xfail and Windows623pass/136skip/1existing-xfail. Applicable Ruff checks pass. Warnings and optional/platform gaps are disclosed, including an unchanged-parent Windows client-session warning. No merge, full CI or performance claim.
